whenToUse: Pick when someone should TALK to the workflow and be spoken back to, in real time, with the model hearing them mid-sentence and able to be interrupted. Reading a script aloud, and transcribing a recording that already exists, are different jobs, because neither needs a live listener.

package.name: openai-realtime
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# OPENAI REALTIME AS A MANIFEST. The first duplex node, and the reason `transport: ws` exists.
#
# WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT from every other node here: it is a CONVERSATION, not a request.
# The socket stays open for the length of a call and both sides write to it. `open` is the
# handshake, `send` reacts to what arrives, `close` is the teardown, and `events` reads inbound
# events exactly as an sse node does.
#
# THE AUDIO LANE IS A SEPARATE SOCKET, in api/audio.yaml, and it exists for ONE reason: MCP
# cannot carry binary audio. Everything else this node produces — transcripts, speech state —
# lands on an output connector and reaches the client over MCP streaming like any other node.

name: openai-realtime
displayName: OpenAI Realtime
description: Live voice conversation with OpenAI's realtime models
version: 2.0.0
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749262616/gravity/icons/ChatGPT-Logo.svg.webp

features:
  - Live two-way voice, with the model interruptible mid-sentence
  - Transcripts of both sides as they happen
  - Semantic or threshold turn detection

allowedHosts:
  - api.openai.com

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [ws]
  executorVersion: ">=1.5.0"

credentials.openaiCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# The SHAPE of the credential, never its value. Transcribed from
# plugin-base/src/credentials/openai.ts, which this package re-exports today.
#
# Values live where they already live: encrypted in Postgres on a deployed universe,
# and in the developer's own .env locally. That is why a manifest is safe to commit.
#
# Nodes reference this by NAME. At run time context.credentials holds EVERY credential
# in the workflow keyed by name, and the executor must select by name, never by
# scanning for the first object with an apiKey: openaiCredential, apolloCredential,
# hunterCredential and searchapiCredential all expose one, so a scan silently
# authenticates against the wrong service the moment a second is added to the
# workflow (04-credentials.md).

name: openaiCredential
displayName: OpenAI (Realtime)
description: Credentials for OpenAI API
documentationUrl: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your OpenAI API key
    placeholder: sk-...

  - name: organizationId
    displayName: Organization ID
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Your OpenAI organization ID (optional)
    placeholder: org-...

  - name: baseUrl
    displayName: Base URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Custom API endpoint (optional)
    default: https://api.openai.com/v1

shared.tools.yaml:
# The OpenAI REALTIME tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does not belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it does not
# belong copied into a node either. It belongs here, exactly as `openai/shared/tools.yaml` holds the
# Responses protocol — imported whole:
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `openai/shared/tools.yaml`. Same vendor, different API, and three real differences
# rather than cosmetic ones:
#
#   the call event   Responses says `response.output_item.done` and needs a `when` to tell a function
#                    call from any other completed item. Realtime has a dedicated
#                    `response.function_call_arguments.done`, so no `when` is needed.
#   no toolsInto     Responses puts the tool list in each REQUEST. A realtime session declares it
#                    ONCE in the handshake, so there is no request field to name; run.yaml reads
#                    `services.mcpService.tools` into session.update itself.
#   no continuity    Responses chains turns with previous_response_id. THE SOCKET IS THE CONTINUITY:
#                    the conversation never ended, so there is nothing to chain.
#
# Also absent, and deliberately: `maxTurns` and `stuckAfterRepeats`. Both count turns, and a turn is
# one model call. Nothing to count here. What bounds a runaway session is the executor's own idle and
# duration ceiling.

# How ONE tool is offered. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }

# How a call ARRIVES. `match` is what makes a stream tractable: events keep coming for the whole
# conversation, and this says which of them is a tool call rather than a transcript or audio.
call:
  match: response.function_call_arguments.done
  id: "return response.call_id"
  name: "return response.name"
  # A JSON STRING, which the executor parses. The trap the schema warns about: passed through
  # unparsed, the tool receives a string where it expected its parameters.
  arguments: "return response.arguments"

# How the result goes BACK. TWO messages, because OpenAI separates them: the output joins the
# conversation, then a response is asked for. Without the second the model holds the result silently.
result: >-
  return [
    { type: 'conversation.item.create',
      item: { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output } },
    { type: 'response.create' }
  ]

files.api/audio.yaml:
$schema: ../../../../_schema/audio.schema.json

# THE AUDIO LANE. The platform's socket to the browser, not the vendor's.
#
# This file exists for ONE reason: MCP cannot carry binary audio. Everything else this node
# produces is in events.yaml and reaches the client over MCP streaming. Nothing non-audio
# should ever be added here.
#
# Every key below NAMES computation the executor does. Rates, byte budgets and which event
# means what — the resampling, the coalescing and the barge-in discard are all identical for
# every vendor, which is exactly why they are not written out here.

in:
  # OpenAI wants 24 kHz; the browser captures 16 kHz. Getting this wrong is not an error
  # anywhere: the model simply hears a chipmunk and it reads as poor accuracy.
  resampleTo: 24000
  message:
    type: input_audio_buffer.append
    audio: "{{ audio.base64 }}"

out:
  match: response.output_audio.delta
  value: "return response.delta"
  # Flushes what is buffered and THEN signals the end. The order is the executor's guarantee:
  # SPEECH_ENDED marks the end of the utterance and the client finishes playback once its queue
  # drains, so a frame sent after it lands on a player that has already stopped.
  done: response.output_audio.done
  # BARGE-IN. Buffered audio is DISCARDED, not flushed, because the person is already talking
  # over the sentence it belongs to.
  interruptOn: input_audio_buffer.speech_started

control:
  # The person pressing hang up. Without this the call only ends when the vendor times out.
  endOn: [END_CALL, stop]

  # THE VENDOR'S VOICE-ACTIVITY DETECTION, forwarded exactly as the retired node forwarded it. The
  # client uses these to show that it is listening.
  #
  # `userSpeaking` names the SAME event as `out.interruptOn` above, and that is deliberate rather
  # than a duplication: one tells the client the person has started talking, the other throws away
  # the assistant audio they talked over. Two different jobs that happen to share a trigger.
  userSpeaking: input_audio_buffer.speech_started
  userStopped: input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped
files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# EVERYTHING HERE REACHES THE CLIENT OVER MCP STREAMING by landing on an output connector. Only
# audio needs the separate lane, and audio is not in this file.

# THE RETIRED NODE'S SHAPE: { query, response } for the last completed turn.
#
# `from: complete` because ONE row sees ONE event, and this needs two: the person's transcript and
# the model's arrive on different events. `complete` fires once at the end over everything already
# emitted, which is the only place both are in scope together.
#
# The retired node emitted this once at the end too (`emitFinal`), so the timing matches.
- emit: text
  from: complete
  value: >-
    return {
      query: (events.filter(e => e.emit === 'userTranscript').map(e => e.value).at(-1)) ?? '',
      response: (events.filter(e => e.emit === 'assistantTranscript').map(e => e.value).at(-1)) ?? ''
    }

# `from: tool` — NOT from the socket. A tool result is produced by the platform running the tool and
# never appears in the vendor's stream, so no `match` could catch it.
- emit: mcpResult
  from: tool
  value: "return { name: call.name, args: call.args, output: call.output }"

# The Q/A log, in the retired node's exact format ("Q1: …\nA1: …\n").
#
# DIFFERENT TIMING, and worth knowing: the retired node appended to this live, turn by turn. One row
# cannot do that here because the two halves of a turn arrive on different events, so this composes
# the whole log at the end instead. Same text, later.
- emit: progress
  from: complete
  value: >-
    return events.filter(e => e.emit === 'userTranscript' || e.emit === 'assistantTranscript')
      .reduce((log, e, i) => log + (e.emit === 'userTranscript' ? 'Q' : 'A')
        + (Math.floor(i / 2) + 1) + ': ' + e.value + '\n', '')

# The handshake was accepted — the node's own liveness signal, and the one thing a fixture can prove
# without a microphone. A REJECTED handshake would otherwise look exactly like a quiet call.
- emit: sessionReady
  match: session.updated
  value: "return true"

- emit: userTranscript
  match: conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed
  value: "return response.transcript || ''"

# ACCUMULATED, so a consumer gets the sentence so far rather than a syllable. The vendor sends one
# delta per few characters; without this a downstream node is handed a word at a time.
- emit: assistantTranscript
  match: response.output_audio_transcript.delta
  value: "return response.delta || ''"
  accumulate: true
  throttleMs: 200
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE duplex session. Not a request: this stays open for the length of the call, and the node's
# run IS the call.
#
# The bearer token goes on the HANDSHAKE, which is why `auth` reads exactly as it does on an
# HTTP call — the executor resolves it through the same code rather than a second copy.

- name: session
  transport: ws
  url: "return 'wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?model=' + config.model"
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.openaiCredential.apiKey }}"

  # THE HANDSHAKE. A list because it is a list for other vendors: Nova needs an ordered
  # sequence here. OpenAI needs exactly one message, so this is a list of one.
  open:
    - type: session.update
      session:
        type: realtime
        model: "{{ config.model }}"
        # AUDIO ONLY. Asking for text as well makes the model write instead of speak on some
        # turns, which on a voice call reads as the assistant going silent.
        output_modalities: [audio]
        instructions: "{{ config.systemPrompt }}"
        max_output_tokens: "return config.maxResponseOutputTokens || 4096"
        audio:
          input:
            # 24 kHz both ways. The client captures at 16 kHz and the executor resamples, which
            # is named in api/audio.yaml rather than done here, because interpolation is not
            # something an expression can express.
            format: { type: audio/pcm, rate: 24000 }
            noise_reduction: { type: near_field }
            transcription: { model: gpt-4o-mini-transcribe }
            # `null` DISABLES turn detection, and that is the vendor's own spelling for it, not
            # an accident of the template. With it null the model never decides the person has
            # finished, so nothing is ever answered unless something else commits the buffer.
            turn_detection: >-
              return config.turnDetection === 'disabled' ? null
                : config.turnDetection === 'server_vad'
                  ? { type: 'server_vad', create_response: true, interrupt_response: true,
                      silence_duration_ms: 700, prefix_padding_ms: 300, threshold: 0.7 }
                  : { type: 'semantic_vad', create_response: true, interrupt_response: true,
                      eagerness: 'high' }
          output:
            format: { type: audio/pcm, rate: 24000 }
            voice: "{{ config.voice }}"

        # TOOLS ARE DECLARED ONCE, HERE, because a realtime session has no per-request moment to
        # offer them the way an HTTP turn does. The executor discovers them from the wired MCP
        # provider before the handshake goes out and puts them in the ordinary consumer root, so
        # this reads `services.mcpService.tools` like any other consumer rather than re-deriving
        # the vendor envelope. That envelope lives once, in shared/tools.yaml.
        #
        # Empty when nothing is wired — the normal case — and the node degrades to a plain voice
        # call rather than failing.
        tools: "return services.mcpService.tools || []"
        tool_choice: "return (services.mcpService.tools || []).length ? 'auto' : 'none'"

    # HISTORY, replayed before the call starts. One entry resolving to an ARRAY of messages, so a
    # variable number of turns is expressible; an empty history resolves to [] and sends nothing.
    #
    # The roles use DIFFERENT content types, which is the vendor's rule and easy to get wrong: a
    # user message carries `input_text`, an assistant message carries `text`.
    - >-
      return (config.conversationHistory || []).map(m => ({
        type: 'conversation.item.create',
        item: {
          type: 'message',
          role: m.role === 'assistant' ? 'assistant' : 'user',
          content: [{ type: m.role === 'assistant' ? 'text' : 'input_text', text: String(m.content ?? '') }]
        }
      }))

    # THE OPENING PROMPT. Two messages: the user message, then `response.create` to make the model
    # answer it immediately. Without the second the item sits in the conversation and the model
    # never speaks, which is the whole point of this field.
    #
    # Resolves to [] when empty, so a call with no opening prompt simply waits for the person.
    - >-
      return String(config.initialRequest || '').trim()
        ? [
            { type: 'conversation.item.create',
              item: { type: 'message', role: 'user',
                      content: [{ type: 'input_text', text: String(config.initialRequest) }] } },
            { type: 'response.create' }
          ]
        : []

  # No `close` list: OpenAI ends a realtime session cleanly on socket close, and sending
  # anything first would be inventing a message the vendor does not document. Nova is the
  # vendor that needs one, which is why the key exists at all.
files.api/toolExchange.yaml:
# The realtime tool protocol, described HERE and not in the platform: the runtime only discovers the
# tools, runs them, and puts the result back on the wire.
#
# Imported WHOLE from the package's shared/ — one file changes when OpenAI changes the wire format.
# No local keys layer on top, because the two dials an HTTP agent sets (`maxTurns`,
# `stuckAfterRepeats`) count TURNS, and a socket has none: the conversation never ended.
$ref: tools
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model, voice, turnDetection]
  properties:
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: Realtime model. Pro for the highest quality, Light for faster and cheaper calls.
      enum: [gpt-realtime-2.1, gpt-realtime-2.1-mini]
      enumNames: [Realtime Pro, Realtime Light]
      default: gpt-realtime-2.1
    systemPrompt:
      type: string
      title: System Prompt
      description: How the model should behave on the call. Shared blocks work here.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    voice:
      type: string
      title: Voice
      description: Which voice the model speaks with
      enum: [alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse, marin, cedar]
      default: alloy
    turnDetection:
      type: string
      title: Turn Detection
      description: >-
        How the model decides the person has finished speaking. Semantic listens for a complete
        thought; Server VAD waits for a fixed silence.
      enum: [semantic_vad, server_vad, disabled]
      enumNames: [Semantic (recommended), Server VAD, Disabled]
      default: semantic_vad
    # RESTORED from the retired node. I had dropped both, and `initialRequest` in particular is not
    # cosmetic: without it the model waits in silence for the person to speak first, so a call opens
    # with nobody saying anything.
    initialRequest:
      type: object
      title: Initial Request
      description: >-
        Sent as a user message the moment the call opens, so the model speaks first. Leave empty and
        the model waits for the person.
      "ui:field": template
    conversationHistory:
      type: object
      title: Conversation History
      description: >-
        Prior turns to replay into the session before the call starts, as an array of
        { role, content }. The model then continues a conversation rather than beginning one.
      "ui:field": template

    maxResponseOutputTokens:
      type: number
      title: Max Response Tokens
      description: Caps how long any single spoken reply can be
      default: 4096
      minimum: 1

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, model, systemPrompt, voice, turnDetection, initialRequest, conversationHistory, maxResponseOutputTokens]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the system prompt
    required: false

outputs:
  # THE RETIRED NODE'S NAMES, restored. I had renamed these wholesale, which orphaned every edge in
  # a saved workflow and every field the voice template reads — the node ran and nothing downstream
  # ever heard from it. An output name IS the contract: it is what someone typed into a template.
  #
  # `conversation` is deliberately NOT restored. The retired node DECLARED it and never emitted to
  # it once, so it was a dot that could not carry anything; lint refuses an output with no row, and
  # reinstating a dead connector to preserve a dead edge is not compatibility.
  - name: text
    type: object
    description: "{ query, response } for the last completed turn: what the person said and what the model answered"
  - name: mcpResult
    type: object
    description: The result of each tool the model called, as { name, args, output }
  - name: progress
    type: string
    description: A running Q/A log of the conversation, in the retired node's format
  - name: sessionReady
    type: boolean
    description: True once the vendor has accepted the session configuration
  - name: userTranscript
    type: string
    description: What the person said, as the model transcribed it
  - name: assistantTranscript
    type: string
    description: What the model said, accumulated as it speaks

credentials:
  # `openaiCredential`, the RETIRED NODE'S NAME, kept deliberately.
  #
  # I first "converged" this on the platform's `openAICredential`, since realtime was the only
  # package ever to use the lower-case spelling. That broke the node outright: a node receives
  # only its OWN declared credentials, and this node's saved config attaches the credential by the
  # old type name, so the bag handed over contained `openaiCredential` while the manifest asked for
  # `openAICredential`. The bearer token resolved to empty and every call failed.
  #
  # A credential name is part of the stored contract, exactly like an output name. Renaming one is
  # a migration with a data change behind it, not a tidy-up.
  - name: openaiCredential
    required: true
    displayName: OpenAI

serviceConnectors:
  # CONSUMES tools, it does not offer them. `isService: false` is what makes this the consumer
  # end, so the canvas draws a serviceConsumer handle and any node providing `mcp` can be wired
  # into it.
  #
  # The service channel and the workflow channel do not cross: tools arrive here, while the
  # transcripts leave on the output connectors.
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: false
    description: MCP tools the model may call mid-conversation, with automatic schema discovery
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: OpenAIRealtimeVoice
kind: CallbackNode

name: OpenAI Realtime Voice
category: Voice
color: "#10A37F"

description: Live two-way voice conversation with OpenAI's realtime models

whenToUse: >-
  Pick when someone should TALK to the workflow and be spoken back to, in real time, with the
  model hearing them mid-sentence and able to be interrupted. Holds one continuous conversation
  for as long as the call lasts and emits both sides as transcripts while it runs. Reading a
  script aloud, and transcribing a recording that already exists, are different jobs, because
  neither needs a live listener.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable, and not even coherently so: there is no single request to reuse. A cached
  # conversation is a contradiction.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# A duplex node cannot be proved by a fixture the way a request can: there is no single reply,
# and nobody is talking. This opens the session, asserts the vendor accepted the handshake, and
# stops. `session.updated` coming back is the one thing a fixture CAN prove without a microphone:
# that the url, the token and every field in the session block were acceptable.
#
# The audio path needs a real call, which is what `unoverse node test` cannot stand in for.

testData:
  config:
    model: gpt-realtime-2.1-mini
    systemPrompt: You are on a test call. Say nothing unless spoken to.
    voice: alloy
    turnDetection: semantic_vad
    initialRequest: "Say the single word: hello"
    maxResponseOutputTokens: 256
  inputs:
    input: {}
  expect:
    sessionReady: "return output.sessionReady === true"
    assistantTranscript: "return output.assistantTranscript.length > 0"
